text:
Emma K: Hey team — just triaging a customer escalation: after last night's model rollout their reranking results for a fixed query changed significantly. Same candidates, same query, different ordering and scores. Customer provided earlier-and-latest pairs. They say this started ~00:30 UTC after we deployed model v3.2.1 rollout 100% to reranker-service.

Mike H: Thanks Emma. Do we have the raw request/response pairs (payloads + scores) and the model ids used for before/after? Need to repro locally.

Emma K: Yes attached in the original support ticket (link: https://redwood.support/ticket/91234). Quick copy: payload (truncated):

```json
{
  "endpoint": "rerank",
  "model": "redwood/reranker-v3.1.9",
  "query": "best running shoes for trail marathons",
  "candidates": ["candA","candB","candC","candD"],
  "top_k": 4
}
```

Before (v3.1.9) scores: [0.78, 0.64, 0.55, 0.21]
After (v3.2.1) scores: [0.62, 0.76, 0.58, 0.18] — notice candA dropped and candB rose, changing order. Customer says this affects UX too much.

Sara L: Two quick hypotheses: 1) normalization semantics changed (we used to return raw logits, now maybe normalized probabilities or a different temperature/softmax). 2) tokenization or candidate embedding mismatch between model variants.

Javier R: Also check quantization/FP changes. v3.2.1 includes a new INT8 quant path for GPU-fast mode; if the hosted rollout switched to a quantized variant by default, small score shifts are expected. But magnitude here (0.14 difference on top result) seems larger than typical qt-noise.

Mike H: Good calls. Emma, can you paste the full request ids + headers (x-request-id) and the exact model tags we served at the time? Also whether the customer used the hosted rerank route or a dedicated/private deployment.

Emma K: From ticket: customer used hosted API (region us-west). Request ids: r_6b2f9a, r_6b2fc3. Model labels in headers: before: redwood/reranker-v3.1.9+2025-11-04, after: redwood/reranker-v3.2.1+2026-02-11. They called /v1/rerank endpoint. No custom normalizer on client side.

Support Bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-4423 (customer-reorder-regression). Assigned to eng-ml.

Javier R: I'll run a deterministic replay harness — handy to force same tokenization, same float precision and compare scores across variants. Emma: can you confirm candidates are the same string-normalized values? If there's whitespace or punctuation differences that could change tokenization.

Emma K: Customer confirmed they canonicalized candidates (lowercase, stripped punctuation) before sending. They filed a small repro bundle with 12 failing queries.

Mike H: Repro script (run locally against our model docker images):

```bash
# fetch model docker images by tag
docker pull registry.redwood.ai/reranker:3.1.9
docker pull registry.redwood.ai/reranker:3.2.1

# run a small python harness
python3 - <<'PY'
import requests
payload = {
  "query": "best running shoes for trail marathons",
  "candidates": ["canda","candb","candc","candd"],
  "top_k": 4
}
for tag in ["3.1.9","3.2.1"]:
  r = requests.post(f"http://localhost:8000/serve/{tag}/rerank", json=payload)
  print(tag, r.json())
PY
```

Sara L: When you do that, check both "score_type" in the response schema. We had a change last quarter where the reranker started returning "score_probability" by default instead of "raw_score" when model returns logits under a certain API flag. Could the hosted routing have flipped that flag?

Javier R: I ran a quick local compare on a subset of queries (using our model images). Results: 3.1.9 raw logits: [3.2, 1.9, 0.8, -1.4] -> softmax -> [0.65,0.24,0.08,0.03]. 3.2.1 raw logits: [2.1, 3.0, 1.1, -1.6] -> softmax -> [0.24,0.67,0.08,0.01]. So the underlying logits actually changed — so it's not only a post-processing normalization difference. That implies model behavior shifted (likely re-training or head-finetune).

Mike H: If logits changed that much, check whether 3.2.1 introduced a candidate-encoding change (embedding table updated or new pooling). Also verify we didn't accidentally swap candidate order when constructing batch tensors (off-by-one).

Emma K: Customer insists inputs were identical. They provided a minimal harness (curl) which I ran against hosted endpoint and reproduced order change. Their payload example: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood/reranker-v3.2.1","query":"best running shoes for trail marathons","candidates":["candA","candB","candC","candD"] }'
```

Response snippet (v3.2.1):
```json
{"scores":[0.62,0.76,0.58,0.18], "order":["candB","candA","candC","candD"], "model":"redwood/reranker-v3.2.1"}
```

Support Bot: Canary deploy log: 2026-02-10 23:50 UTC — rollout to 100% for model tag redwood/reranker-v3.2.1; kernel path: int8_gpu_opt; config flags: {"score_output":"probability","normalize_candidates":true}.

Sara L: Aha — config flag "normalize_candidates":true could change candidate embeddings if it's a preprocessing step that alters text. If the flag was accidentally toggled in hosted serving config, it would affect results even if model weights identical. We need to audit the deploy config history.

Javier R: I'll diff the preprocessing between the two container images and run unit tests for tokenizer + encoder outputs on the failing candidates. If preprocessing differs, that explains it. If preprocessing is same, then it's a model-weight/attention change.

Mike H: Action items: 1) Eng-ML (Javier) to diff preprocessing and encoder outputs — target EOD. 2) Eng-Infra to roll back hosted routing to the previous model variant for customer region if we confirm regression — Sara will coordinate rollback. 3) CS (Emma) to send the 12 failing queries to eng-ml and request customer permission for an internal repro run. 4) If root cause is config flag flip, we need a postmortem + gating in deploy pipeline to prevent accidental config drift.

Emma K: Noted. Customer asked for ETA and whether we can pin them to older model while we investigate. Sara, can we do a per-customer pin?

Sara L: Yes, we can add a model_version override per API key. I'll provision a temporary override for their API key and route their requests to v3.1.9 within the hour.

Javier R: Quick preliminary result — tokenization is identical. Encoder embeddings differ: calling encoder.forward on candidate strings returns different vectors between images (L2 diff ~0.12 avg). That suggests either an embedding matrix change or a different random seed in initialization for newly trained head. Will look into commit history for v3.2.1.

Mike H: If it's a model-change regression, we need a quality gate on reranker head changes; we should add a small automated regression suite that runs a fixed set of queries comparing candidate ranking stability before rollout. This would've caught it. I'll open a ticket in eng-releases.

Support Bot: Follow-up: assigned INC-2026-4423 -> eng-ml, SLO: update customer within 6 hours.

Emma K: I'll keep the customer updated and confirm whether the temporary pin helps. Will also collect any additional failing examples. Thanks all.

Sara L: FYI — I'm scheduling a quick 15-min sync at 14:30 UTC to confirm rollback/pin and next steps.

Mike H: Thanks. Keep notes in the incident. If it's a config drift, patch pipeline; if model regression, block rollout and run regression harness.

Emma K: Closing for now — will post updates in this thread as we make progress. :thumbsup:
